articles.title: Steve Sarkisian Calls Out Colin Simmons for Miming Urinating During Celebration in Texas' Win
articles.summary: Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian wasn't a fan of defensive end Colin Simmons utilizing a sack celebration in which he pretended to urinate during the No. 1 Longhorns' 20-17 win over No. 14 Tennessee on Saturday.
articles.body:
Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian wasn't a fan of defensive end Colin Simmons utilizing a sack celebration in which he pretended to urinate during the No. 1 Longhorns' 20-17 win over No. 14 Tennessee on Saturday.

"It can't happen," Sarkisian told reporters after the game. "That's a bad football play. We had harped and talked about this game, about not getting emotional with the crowd. That was an emotional play. We had a couple others that were close too, so we had a real talk about it at halftime. About how we needed to play in the second half, we needed to celebrate with one another."

Simmons received a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for the celebration, which occurred after he took down Volunteers quarterback Faizon Brandon in the second quarter of the contest.

While the sack occurred on third down and would have forced a Tennessee punt, the penalty kept the drive alive. The Volunteers moved into Texas' territory on the same possession, but ultimately turned the ball over on downs.

Tennessee later tied the game in the third quarter, although Texas moved back in front with a field goal and eventually held on for the win to stay unbeaten at 4-0.

Despite the penalty, Simmons put together a dominant performance in the victory.

He finished with five sacks, tying the all-time single-game record for the program (h/t ESPN's Peter Burns ). Simmons recorded back-to-back sacks in the third quarter of the contest, but didn't celebrate after either play.

The 20-year-old has continued to serve as a key piece of Texas' defense this year after amassing 12 sacks in 2025. He racked up four tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss and two sacks across three games heading into Saturday's action.

Simmons was listed as the No. 3 overall prospect in the 2027 NFL draft class on the latest big board from Bleacher Report's NFL Scouting Department.

articles.title: Como si ahora quisieran ser la mejor selección de la historia...
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Inglaterra - España
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Inglaterra - España
articles.body: No es un Mundial, pero la Liga de las Naciones también mola. Posiblemente, el mejor invento de la UEFA en mucho tiempo. Muchísimo mejor, desde luego, que aquellos amistosos entre España y Macedonia. Gracias a esto la segunda estrella se estrenó en Wembley, el templo del fútbol de selecciones en Europa. Templo conquistado una vez más por un equipo que mantiene el hambre por ganar. Porque Inglaterra exigió la mejor versión de España, que la sacó al inicio y al final del partido para protagonizar una espectacular remontada. También dejó la sensación, y que no se enfade nadie, que una final contra Inglaterra habría sido aún más difícil que contra Argentina. Pero eso ya es pasado. Lo que cuenta ahora es que España sigue teniendo ambición. La misma que Luis de la Fuente se encarga de alimentar, sin dejar que nadie se relaje. Como si tras el Mundial quisieran ser la mejor selección de la historia... ¿Y por qué no? Con Lamine en la presión, a Guehi no se le ocurrió otra cosa que girarse en la frontal del área buscando aún no se sabe bien qué, si un pase al portero o un regate. El central de Inglaterra terminó perdiendo la pelota y dejando a Lamine en el mano a mano con Trafford para que hiciera el 0-1. Era el minuto 1 y la cara de Tuchel era de querer sacarle del campo de inmediato. El chico no se volvería a complicar en todo el partido. Wembley, dos estrellas en el pecho, Kane enfrente, el Balón de Oro dentro de un mes... Lamine tenía el escaparate perfecto y saltó al terreno de juego a divertirse. Gol en el minuto uno y jugón cada vez que entró en contacto con la pelota. En el 34' dejó un pase a Olmo de tacón que levantó hasta los gritos de admiración de la afición inglesa. Una genialidad al alcance de muy pocos. España encajó en cuatro minutos en Wembley más goles que en todo el Mundial de Estados Unidos. Gordon y Kane dieron la vuelta al marcador entre el 36' y el 40' y acabaron con el paraíso defensivo en el que vivía la selección desde el pasado verano. En el Mundial, solo Bélgica por medio de De Ketelaere fue capaz de batir a Unai Simón, que tuvo mucho más trabajo que ayer en todo el Mundial. Porque además del penalti fallado por Kane, el portero tuvo que intervenir en tres ocasiones. Se tiende a buscar culpables en cada gol encajado por un equipo y el tanto logrado por Gordon para empatar a uno fue de los que se analizan al detalle. Que si Nico no puede perder el balón ahí, que si cerraba el jugador más lento (Fabián), que si Cucurella se deja superar... Y la realidad es que Inglaterra armó una contra de libro perfectamente culminada por Gordon. Volvió el fútbol de selecciones y lo disfrutamos sin la pausa publicitaria que nos colaron en el Mundial. Y qué bendición. El cooling break en el Inglaterra-España habría cortado el ritmo de un partidazo, jugado con un ritmo altísimo durante los 90 minutos. Confiemos en que UEFA mantenga esta política durante la Eurocopa que se disputará en 2028 en Reino Unido. El gol del triunfo llevó el sello, como tantas veces, de Mikel Oyarzabal. El delantero de la Real empezó el duelo en el banquillo, pero salió en la segunda parte para darle el triunfo a la selección en Wembley. Su definición en el 2-3 fue una maravilla, levantando el balón por encima de Trafford tras un gran pase de Baena. No hay duda de que España tiene en Oyarzabal delantero para rato.

articles.title: No. 1 Texas survives penalties, special teams errors to stave off miraculous comeback bid from No. 14 Tennessee
articles.summary: The Longhorns committed 11 penalties and allowed both a punt return touchdown as well as an onside kick recovery.
articles.body:
That hardly tells the story of a near collapse that would have been bigger than the Lone Star State.

The top-ranked Longhorns had to sweat out a 20-17 victory in Knoxville after going up 10 points with 5:41 remaining. In the game's final act, No. 1 Texas (4-0, 1-0 SEC) allowed No. 14 Tennessee (3-1, 0-1) to go the length of the field for a touchdown and recover a subsequent onside kick.

That set up a potential game-tying or game-winning drive for the Volunteers in a vivacious Neyland Stadium that included U.S. president Donald Trump .

Texas held on and emerged from its first conference bout unscathed, albeit after 11 penalties, two turnovers and a collection of special teams miscues, one of which resulted in a Tennessee punt return touchdown.

Arch Manning, who hit on only half of his pass attempts last week in a win over UTSA, couldn't miss early this time around.

He completed his first seven passes for 120 yards against Tennessee, the alma mater of his uncle, Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning .

Arch Manning, a Heisman Trophy hopeful and an intriguing NFL Draft prospect, attacked Jim Knowles' Volunteers defense from the get-go.

Even if it was underthrown, his deep ball for wide receiver Emmett Mosley V amounted to a 43-yard pickup on the game-opening drive . Running back Raleek Brown carried the momentum with a 9-yard rushing touchdown.

On Texas' third series, Manning found wideout Ryan Wingo twice, first over the middle for 15 yards and then on a dump-off that saw the elusive Wingo author a 14-yard gain. Two plays after that, Manning uncorked one of the prettier throws of his Longhorns career, a perfectly placed 29-yard strike to wide receiver Jermaine Bishop Jr. that soared outside the reach of over-pursuing Tennessee defensive back Qua Moss.

Although Steve Sarkisian's team couldn't tack on another touchdown in the red zone, Texas came away with a field goal to go up 10-3.

The score remained that way the rest of the first half.

Penalties and ball-security issues cost the Longhorns, whereas Josh Heupel's Volunteers were stifled by Texas' unrelenting pressure.

Tennessee freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon took a bevy of hits; however, the one that knocked him out of the game for a series and change wasn't sustained on a pass play.

On a quarterback power early in the second quarter, Brandon — a dual-threat QB who was the Rivals industry ranking's No. 10 overall prospect in the 2026 class — veered right.

In no time, though, he was swarmed by Texas linebackers Rasheem Biles and Justin Cryer. There was no gain on the play, but what the Vols lost, at least temporarily, was their signal-caller.

In Brandon's absence, Manning tossed an interception and nearly committed an additional turnover. The pick stemmed from Manning taking a chance on a play-action fake that didn't really get the safety to bite. He rolled the dice anyway, firing downfield into double coverage. Cornerback Kayin Lee tracked the pass and pried it away from wide receiver Cam Coleman at the doorstep of the end zone.

Soon after the lone full series Tennessee backup George MacIntyre quarterbacked, a high snap flew through the hands of Manning. Somehow, he recovered the fumble, except the 12-yard loss ruined what turned out to be a three-and-out.

Once Simmons finished off a 16-yard sack that would have dropped Tennessee to a fourth-and-29 on its own 12-yard line, he received an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty "for simulating using the restroom."

While Simmons pretending to urinate on Shields–Watkins Field didn't lead to Tennessee points, it did cost Texas great field position before intermission.

Simmons redeemed himself with his sack-filled performance, during which he chased down Brandon for three second-half sacks. Texas' defense, as a whole, clocked out with 10 sacks.

Manning, who was 14 of 19 with 201 passing yards and the aforementioned pick, was sacked six times.

The third phase of the game made things interesting.

Vols punter Jackson Ross pinned Texas at its 6-yard line in the infancy of the third quarter. Four snaps later, Moss returned a Longhorns punt 57 yards to the house to knot things up 10-10.

Texas had a response, and it came from Manning and one of his most heralded receivers, Coleman, who laid out to make a highlight-reel 30-yard grab . Manning lofted the pass while weathering a hit that drew an unnecessary roughness penalty.

That sequence put the Longhorns in position for a 44-yard field goal that made it a 13-10 game.

Texas briefly seized command of the game midway through the fourth quarter. A third-and-8 hookup between Manning and Wingo slingshotted the Longhorns. Those two connected again before Texas turned to the ground game.

Just like he did in the opening frame, Brown found pay dirt.

Tennessee turned the ball over on downs its next drive, then used all three of its timeouts to pave the way for a last-ditch effort.

After struggling offensively all afternoon, Brandon orchestrated a 10-play, 80-yard touchdown drive. A 16-yard run from Brandon on third-and-12 was critical. It was the catalyst for a 30-yard touchdown pass to Mike Matthews .

Suddenly, Tennessee had a bit more than a minute to tie or take the lead.

Yet a sloppy final drive concluded with a heave to the end zone that Texas' Jelani McDonald broke up to seal the road win and prevent a Vols miracle.

articles.title: Yamal nets in Spain’s 3-2 comeback win against England in Nations League
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal goal opens the scoring, but Spain made to comeback in Nations League win as Harry Kane misses penalty.
articles.body:
World champions Spain came from behind to beat England 3-2 in an entertaining Nations League encounter at Wembley on Saturday, denying the hosts a cathartic win after their painful World Cup exit.

Victory for Luis de la Fuente’s men extends Spain’s astonishing unbeaten run to 39 matches – a record for a European team.

Thomas Tuchel’s men got off to a nightmare start when Lamine Yamal pounced on a gaffe by defender Marc Guehi, and they could easily have been three goals down as silky Spain created multiple chances.

But England, criticised for their ultra-defensive tactics in their World Cup semifinal defeat to Argentina, showed adventure of their own and got their reward in the 36th minute when Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon finished a fine team move.

Four minutes later, the home side were ahead after Kane headed home Nico O’Reilly’s cross via a Marc Cucurella deflection.

Kane had a golden chance to give England a two-goal cushion from the penalty spot 10 minutes into the second half but slipped slightly, crashing his shot against the bar.

Spain, who beat England in the Euro 2024 final, took full advantage, with substitutes Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal putting their side ahead, taking advantage of more sloppy defensive play from the home side.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was adamant ahead of the match that it did not signal a new start, but he will have been dismayed by his team’s nervy start.

Manchester City’s Guehi, with a chance to clear in the second minute, inexplicably turned back towards goalkeeper James Trafford, apparently unaware that Yamal was just behind him.

The teenager collected the ball and curled a left-footed effort off the inside of the post.

Ferran Torres was in the thick of the action, with an effort ruled out for offside and another shot saved by Trafford, in for longtime number one Jordan Pickford.

He also squandered a golden opportunity with just the goalkeeper to beat.

Yamal then set up Dani Olmo, who flashed wide as Spain rued yet another miss.

England, who had shown plenty of promise down the wings, made the visitors pay with an incisive counter-attacking goal after winning the ball back deep in their own half.

Gordon was involved early in the move and surged forward, collecting Jude Bellingham’s pass to steer the ball decisively past goalkeeper Unai Simon.

And, with the atmosphere now totally changed, England were in front when Kane rose to head home.

Tuchel’s men started the second half brightly and had a chance to extend their lead from the spot when they were awarded a penalty for a Rodri foul on Bellingham following a VAR check.

But Kane crashed his shot against the bar, and England paid the price when Baena steered home on the hour mark after O’Reilly had given the ball away to Olmo.

Worse was to come for the home side when Baena turned provider for Oyarzabal, who dinked the ball over Trafford.

articles.title: England 2-3 Spain: World champions win at Wembley in Nations League despite Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane goals
articles.summary: Report from Wembley as Lamine Yamal, Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal help Spain to thrilling victory in Nations League; European and world champions show their class despite Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane giving Three Lions lead; Crucially, Kane slipped and hit a penalty against the bar
articles.body:
It was the World Cup final that might have been had England not squandered their advantage against Argentina this summer - but Spain showed the gap in quality in a result which is a major blow to Thomas Tuchel's stated aim of winning this competition.

Bad errors from Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly helped Lamine Yamal and Alex Baena score Spain's first two and England were cut open through the match, including for Mikel Oyarzabal's winner which came with 16 minutes to play.

But while England's defence suffered, there was brilliant forward play, too.

Anthony Gordon had urged England to lean into their traditional strengths this week and they did just that with an exceptional counter-attack to make it 1-1, which saw the winger combine with Jude Bellingham before precisely applying the finish. Harry Kane's header from O'Reilly's cross made it 2-1 and capped an incredible transformation in the match.

In four minutes, Spain had conceded more goals than in their eight World Cup games combined.

There was then a pivotal moment, when England were awarded a penalty at the start of the second half, when Rodri was judged to have fouled Bellingham, following a VAR check. But Kane slipped and sent his spot-kick against the bar - and Spain capitalised.

Ferran Torres may have passed up two one-on-one chances in the first half, but Spain were clinical after the missed spot-kick to go top of Nations League Group A3.

With this result, Spain's record-breaking unbeaten streak is also extended to 39 games. England will now have to find a way to beat them in Madrid in November - and win against Czech Republic and Croatia in the meantime - if they are to make it to the Nations League finals and show they are capable of toppling the best when it matters.

2: GOAL! Marc Guehi's blunder allows Lamine Yamal to take the ball, run in on goal and score. An early gift for the world champions!

9: NO GOAL! Ferran Torres heads in after a corner which comes from a Myles Lewis-Skelly misplaced pass. But the Spain forward is flagged offside.

16: BIG SAVE! James Trafford saves a one-on-one with Ferran Torres after England's defence is cut wide open.

27: HUGE CHANCE! But Ferran Torres sends his shot wide of the goal after Rodri plays him in following a Lamine Yamal interception from Elliot Anderson's pass.

36: GOAL! Anthony Gordon combines with Jude Bellingham before completing an exceptional counter-attack move to level the match.

39: SO CLOSE! Harry Kane drops to his knees as his shot flies narrowly wide as England almost grab a quickfire second. The home fans inside Wembley roar their team forwards.

40: ENGLAND LEAD! An incredible transformation in mood, momentum and scoreline as Kane heads in Nico O'Reilly's cross despite Marc Cucurella's attempts to block.

45: CROSSBAR! Cucurella's mis-hit cross kisses the face of the England crossbar.

54: PENALTY MISS! Rodri is punished after a VAR check for his challenge on Bellingham in the box… but Kane slips as he takes the spot-kick and fires it against the bar!

60: GOAL! Spain punish Kane's miss when they pounce on an error from O'Reilly and tee up sub Alex Baena to clip in the equaliser from the edge of the box.

74: GOAL! England drop deep under pressure but it's a through pass from Baena which releases Mikel Oyarzabal to tuck away the eventual winner.

Analysis: A statement win slips away from England

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett at Wembley:

"One captain's slip, one memorable scalp that slipped away. A missed penalty and a missed opportunity for England. Though it's hard to argue that Spain weren't the far superior side over 90 minutes.

"The world champions could have been out of sight within 30 minutes, after a dominant display of their prowess. And a couple of self-destructive England passes. The fact that Spain were only a goal ahead, gave England hope and it was a brilliant 10-minute spell that saw England grab the lead. Firstly a brilliant goal from their best player on the night, Anthony Gordon, and then from captain Kane with a header.

"The home side started the second half really well but when Kane missed from the spot to give England a two-goal lead, Spain sensed blood. Their response with strikes from Yamal and Baena was decisive and deserved.

"A defeat with some merit then, for Tuchel's England. But there still seemed to be a gulf in class."
